```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
```

## Problem 1

```{r}
data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r}
ny_noaa |>
  summarize(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ mean(is.na(.))
    )
  )
```

The `ny_noaa` dataset contains 2,595,176 observations and 7 variables. Key variables include weather station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, maximum temperature, and minimum temperature. Missing data are an important issue in this dataset, especially for maximum and minimum temperature, which are missing for approximately 44% of observations. Snow depth is missing for about 23% of observations, snowfall for about 15%, and precipitation for about 6%.


```{r}
ny_noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(format(date, "%Y")),
    month = as.integer(format(date, "%m")),
    day = as.integer(format(date, "%d")),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10
  )
```

```{r}
ny_noaa |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE)
```

The most commonly observed snowfall value is 0 mm, which occurs far more often than any other value because most days do not have snowfall. Other frequently observed values include 25 mm, 13 mm, 51 mm, and 76 mm.



```{r}
jan_july_temp =
  ny_noaa |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = recode(
      month,
      `1` = "January",
      `7` = "July"
    )
  )
```


```{r}
ggplot(
  jan_july_temp,
  aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~month) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)",
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature by Station in January and July"
  )
```

Average maximum temperatures are substantially lower in January than in July. January temperatures show more variability across stations and years, while July temperatures are generally concentrated around the upper 20s °C. There is no clear monotonic trend over time in either month, although several unusually low observations are visible and may represent outliers or unusual station-year conditions.



```{r}
ggplot(
  ny_noaa,
  aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)
) +
  geom_bin_2d() +
  labs(
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)",
    title = "Maximum vs Minimum Temperature"
  )
```

There is a strong positive relationship between minimum and maximum temperature. Most observations are concentrated along a diagonal band, indicating that warmer days tend to have both higher minimum and maximum temperatures. A small number of observations appear far from the main concentration and may represent extreme weather events or unusual measurements.


```{r}
ny_noaa |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = snow, group = year)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)",
    title = "Distribution of Snowfall Values Between 0 and 100 mm by Year"
  )
```
The distribution of snowfall values between 0 and 100 mm is fairly similar across years, with no clear long-term shift in the overall pattern. Most snowfall observations are concentrated at lower to moderate values, with several repeated peaks corresponding to commonly observed snowfall amounts.

## Problem 2


```{r}
nhanes_covar =
  read_csv(
    "data/nhanes_covar.csv",
    skip = 4
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names()
```

```{r}
nhanes_accel =
  read_csv("data/nhanes_accel.csv") |>
  janitor::clean_names()
```
```{r}
nhanes_covar =
  nhanes_covar |>
  mutate(
    sex = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c(1, 2),
      labels = c("male", "female")
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "Less than high school",
        "High school equivalent",
        "More than high school"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    age >= 21,
    !is.na(sex),
    !is.na(age),
    !is.na(bmi),
    !is.na(education)
  )

nhanes_df =
  nhanes_covar |>
  inner_join(
    nhanes_accel,
    by = "seqn"
  )
```


```{r}
nhanes_df |>
  count(education, sex) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Number of Men and Women in Each Education Category"
  )
```
```{r}
ggplot(
  nhanes_df,
  aes(x = age, fill = sex)
) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~education) +
  labs(
    x = "Age",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Sex",
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education Level"
  )
```

The number of men and women is fairly similar in the less than high school and more than high school education groups, while the high school equivalent group contains more men than women. The age distributions also differ across education levels. Participants with more than a high school education tend to be younger, particularly among women, while participants in the high school equivalent group tend to be older.

```{r}
nhanes_df =
  nhanes_df |>
  mutate(
    total_activity = rowSums(
      across(min1:min1440),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
```



```{r}
ggplot(
  nhanes_df,
  aes(
    x = age,
    y = total_activity,
    color = sex
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~education) +
  labs(
    x = "Age",
    y = "Total Daily Activity",
    color = "Sex",
    title = "Total Daily Activity by Age, Sex, and Education Level"
  )
```
Total daily activity generally decreases with age, although the pattern differs somewhat across education groups. In the less than high school group, activity declines noticeably at older ages for both men and women. In the high school equivalent group, activity is relatively high among younger adults and then decreases with age. In the more than high school group, activity levels are fairly stable through middle age and decline at older ages. Differences between men and women vary across age and education groups rather than following one consistent pattern.


```{r}
activity_long =
  nhanes_df |>
  select(seqn, sex, education, min1:min1440) |>
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute",
    values_to = "activity"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    minute = as.numeric(str_remove(minute, "min"))
  )
```

```{r}
activity_long |>
  group_by(education, sex, minute) |>
  summarize(
    mean_activity = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = minute,
      y = mean_activity,
      color = sex
    )
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~education) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 360, 720, 1080, 1440),
    labels = c("12 AM", "6 AM", "12 PM", "6 PM", "12 AM")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time of Day",
    y = "Average Activity",
    color = "Sex",
    title = "24-Hour Activity Patterns by Sex and Education Level"
  )
```
Across all three education groups, activity is lowest overnight, rises sharply in the morning, remains relatively high during the daytime, and declines again in the evening. Women generally show slightly higher average activity than men during much of the daytime, although the size of the difference varies across education groups and time of day.
